groups.text:
For each question from 16 to 20, choose the word closest in meaning to the underlined word(s).

Father had made up his mind. "Ellen will be taking care of you. Stop your whining right now! Nothing will change my mind!" he said with __(16: finality)__.
I sensed my life was about to change __(17: drastically)__ when Ellen began taking charge of me. Father __(18: confirmed)__ my worst fears when he added, "Shu Ma will leave tonight." They were getting rid of my Shu Ma just like other families getting rid of servants who had __(19: outlived)__ their usefulness.
"I don't want Ellen! I don't like her!" I cried. "I want Shu Ma!"
Ever kind and patient, Ellen bit her lip and put on a brave face even in my stormiest moments. Father was less understanding. "We'll see about that, young man," he growled __(20: sullenly)__. I knew then that I had better stop throwing my tantrums.
Adapted from 'Things That Must Not Be Forgotten – A Childhood in Wartime China' by Michael David Kwan

++Text 2++
The extract below is taken from an online article.
Wearing the right shoes is important for every runner whether they are experienced athletes or beginners. A shoe's weight is just one of several factors runners should consider. Good running shoes do more than keep the feet comfortable. They play a key role in helping runners perform well and in preventing injuries.
Firstly, proper running shoes provide strong support and sufficient cushioning. When a runner's feet hit the ground, the shoes help to absorb the impact. This reduces pressure on the feet, ankles and knees, making running safer. It also lowers the risk of common injuries such as sprains, muscle strain and joint pain.
In addition, running shoes are designed to help the body move correctly. They improve balance and support smoother, more controlled movements while running. With better stability and posture, runners can run for longer periods without discomfort.
In conclusion, choosing the right pair of running shoes may seem like a simple decision but that is far from the truth. Think about the features that will suit you best. Not every runner needs shoes with all sorts of fancy features. The right shoes help runners enjoy their runs, improve their performance and protect their bodies from injury.

groups.text:
There are 10 blanks, numbered 26 to 35, in the passage below. From the list of words given, choose the most suitable word for each blank. Write its letter (A to Q) in the blank. The letters (I) and (O) have been omitted to avoid confusion during marking.
**EACH WORD CAN BE USED ONLY ONCE.**
[[table1]]

For thousands of years, people have admired ivory for its beauty and strength.
During the Stone Age, ivory from the mammoth, an extinct ancestor of the elephant, __(26)__ used to make household items, tools, weapons and ornaments. Durable, smooth, easy to carve and cool __(27)__ the touch, ivory was considered a valuable material. It was __(28)__ precious that many people referred to it as "white gold".
Before plastic was invented, ivory was carved into many useful and decorative objects, __(29)__ as chopsticks, musical instruments and furniture. Even after plastic became widely available, wealthy people continued to use ivory as ornaments __(30)__ they regarded it as a symbol of wealth and prestige.
As demand for ivory increased, it became highly sought __(31)__. African elephants, which generally have larger and heavier tusks than __(32)__ Asian counterparts, became the main targets of poachers. Although there is now an international ban __(33)__ the ivory trade, illegal hunting still continues in many parts of the world.
__(34)__ stronger efforts are made to protect these animals, conservationists fear that African elephants could disappear __(35)__ the next twenty years.
Protecting endangered animals is everyone's responsibility if we want future generations to enjoy the rich diversity of wildlife.
Adapted from "Little Red Dot 29 Aug 2006"

Each of the underlined words contains either a spelling or grammatical error. Write the correct word in each of the boxes.

Janet stood in the middle of the stage, starting her speech. She had often wondered why people listened spellbound whenever Dave, her brother, spoke. She was __(36: begin)__ to understand that it was not just the way he spoke but how he said it. A flick of the wrist here, a pause there, a sudden unexpected smile and his listeners were __(37: cabtivatted)__. Practising her own speech over the last week, Janet had incorporated some of his skills. She refused to give in to her __(38: nervous)__ this time.
Now as Janet spoke about the drought in the village, she knew how to modulate her voice, when to pause for effect, even to __(39: jescher)__ a little with her hands. __(40: Eloquent)__, she talked of the poor harvest, of her father's __(41: daspparate)__ needs to make ends meet and of her father's sacrifices for his children. At only one point did she __(42: foltor)__. When she started to describe her father while standing behind the podium, she __(43: stammer)__ and could not continue.
A __(44: fimilair)__ face had appeared in the audience. Instinctively, Janet raised her right hand and pointed in his direction. "He's the reason why I am speaking here today!" The audience erupted __(45: to)__ a roar. "That's my father!"
Adapted from "Rice Without Rain" by Minfong Ho

Fill in each blank with a suitable word.

Singapore imports much of its food because of its small land size.
The country's __(46)__ land means that local farms cannot produce enough food to feed the entire population. As a result, Singapore depends heavily on __(47)__ food from many different countries. __(48)__, unexpected events such as extreme weather, global conflicts or disruptions to transport routes may make food supplies more __(49)__ to interruptions. These events could even lead to temporary food __(50)__ in some parts of the world.
To strengthen food security, Singapore has invested in __(51)__ farming methods that make better use of every available space. One example is vertical farming, where vegetables are grown on stacked shelves __(52)__ of across wide fields. This allows farmers to produce a larger __(53)__ of crops while using much less land.
Many farms also rely on modern farming techniques. Sensors monitor light, temperature and humidity so that crops receive the __(54)__ amount of water and nutrients. As a result, farmers can __(55)__ the growth of their crops while avoiding unnecessary waste of water and energy.
Some farms recycle water and use it more efficiently, helping to __(56)__ valuable natural resources. Since the vegetables are grown locally, they reach supermarkets more __(57)__, allowing consumers to enjoy greater freshness than vegetables transported __(58)__ long distances.
Although local farms cannot meet the entire __(59)__ for food, they play an important role in building a more __(60)__ food supply for Singapore's future.
Urban farming demonstrates how careful planning, technology and innovation can help Singapore prepare for future challenges.
Written by: Alvin Soh

Read the passage and answer questions 66 to 75.

**1** In the ancient kingdom of Tiwana, two cousins, Trev and Dev, trained under the kingdom's most respected sculptor, Master Govin. Although they trained together from a young age, they were very different. Trev's extraordinary natural talent quickly earned him the admiration of visitors but years of praise had made him proud. He became dismissive of weaker apprentices and was determined to prove he was the best. He was unbothered by the words and feelings of others. Dev, however, lacked Trev's natural brilliance. His early sculptures were rough and uneven but he was patient and hardworking. Whenever Master Govin corrected him, Dev listened carefully. He observed experienced craftsmen, practised tirelessly and gradually improved.
**2** One summer, the King of Tiwana announced a competition to select a sculpture for the new Hall of Wisdom. The winner would receive a royal title and a chest of gold. While many sculptors saw it as a chance to showcase their skills, Trev saw **this** as an opportunity to earn fame.
**3** Ignoring Master Govin's advice to focus on the craft rather than recognition, Trev chose a huge slab of marble and began carving a towering warrior dressed in elaborate armour. His sculpture was designed to impress. Dev took a different approach. Before touching his tools, he spent several days travelling through villages and marketplaces, observing ordinary people. He watched labourers working under the scorching sun and parents caring for their children. Inspired by what he had seen, he decided to sculpt an elderly farmer carrying a tired child on his shoulders.
**4** As the weeks passed, Trev worked hastily. Whenever cracks or uneven surfaces appeared, he concealed them under carvings instead of repairing them properly. Trev was only concerned with the sculpture's appearance. He paid little attention to its durability. "People will regard my work highly no matter what," he said to himself, smirking with pride. Meanwhile, Dev worked steadily. Rather than focussing on impressing others, he carefully carved the farmer's weathered hands, tired posture and gentle expression. His sculpture was simple but every detail reflected patience and care. When visitors entered the workshop to watch them work, they gravitated towards Trev's spectacular warrior. Seeing **this**, Trev mocked his cousin's ordinary subject. "Your sculpture is not getting you anything. Your common man pales in comparison to my towering warrior," he scoffed. "Sometimes," Dev replied calmly, "ordinary things are what matter most."
**5** Finally, the day of judgement arrived. The palace courtyard was filled with spectators who were excited to find out which sculpture would make it to the Hall of Wisdom. Both sculptures had their own set of admirers. The judges decided to assess Trev's sculpture first. However, just as they were inspecting it, a faint crack echoed through the courtyard. Moments later, a large fracture spread across the statue's chest before both of its arms broke away. Trev's face turned beetroot red and he lowered his head as the broken pieces lay scattered across the ground. The hidden flaws he had covered up had finally been exposed. Later that afternoon, the judges announced Dev as the winner. Although his sculpture lacked grandeur, it moved everyone. The judges praised the patience, craftsmanship and understanding reflected in every detail.
**6** That evening, Trev returned to the workshop and studied Dev's sculpture. For the first time, he noticed the warmth in the farmer's eyes, the careful shaping of **his** worn hands and the quiet beauty that could only come from patience. Seeing that, realisation finally dawned on him; it was never just about the end result. Master Govin then came into the workshop and reminded him, "Young man, the competition has never been about producing the most impressive sculpture. It was about becoming the kind of sculptor capable of creating one."
**7** From that day on, Trev understood that his greatest failure had not been losing the competition but believing that success was measured by recognition alone. Years later, people no longer remembered the royal prize. Instead, they remembered the sculptor who had allowed the journey to shape both his masterpiece and his character.
Written by: Rubinder Kaur

questions.stem: Michael is most upset about the cancelled party plans and so __________ Peter.

explanation: Rule: to say that something is also true of another person, use so + helping verb + subject. The helping verb is the same one, in the same tense, as in the first half of the sentence.
The first half says 'Michael **is** most upset', which is present tense, so the helping verb is a present form of 'to be'. That rules out 'was' and 'were'.
The verb must agree with the subject that comes after it. 'Peter' is one person, so we need the singular 'is', not 'are'.
'...and so is Peter.' The answer is option (1).

questions.stem: "Lisa has the entire series of the limited Minecraft Collection, __________ she?" I asked.

explanation: Rule: a positive statement takes a negative question tag, and the tag uses the helping verb of the statement.
Here 'has' is the main verb meaning 'owns' (present simple), not a helping verb. There is no 'has + past participle'. A present simple main verb takes do/does in the tag.
'Lisa' is singular, so we need 'doesn't', not 'don't'.
'hasn't' is tempting, but it is used when 'has' is a helping verb, as in 'Lisa has collected the series, hasn't she?'. The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: "Ashvin, you only need to prepare for the presentation. Get your groupmates to complete the project by __________," Mrs Tan said.

explanation: Rule: a reflexive pronoun (-self, -selves) must match the person doing the action.
Who is to complete the project? 'Your groupmates'. They are plural and are being talked about (third person), so the pronoun is 'themselves'.
'yourselves' is tempting because Mrs Tan is speaking to Ashvin, but Ashvin is not the one completing the project. He only prepares for the presentation.
'...complete the project by themselves.' The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: There is __________ hope of finding the missing wallet before the mall closes.

explanation: 'Hope' is an uncountable noun here: the verb is the singular 'is' and there is no 's' on 'hope'.
'few' and 'many' are only used with countable plural nouns (few coins, many wallets), so they are out.
'any' is used in negative sentences and questions ('There isn't any hope'), not in a positive statement like this one.
'little' goes with uncountable nouns and means 'almost no'. 'There is little hope...' The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: __________ harsh your coach may sound, please be assured that he has the best interest of the team at heart.

explanation: Look at what comes right after the blank: an adjective ('harsh') and then the subject and verb ('your coach may sound').
The pattern However + adjective + subject + verb means 'no matter how'. 'However harsh your coach may sound' = 'No matter how harsh your coach may sound'.
'Although' is tempting because the meaning is close, but it needs the normal word order: 'Although your coach may sound harsh, ...'.
'Regardless' needs 'of how', and 'Nevertheless' starts a new sentence. The answer is option (1).

questions.stem: A number of students from that class __________ to be stationed at the booths for the upcoming fund-raising carnival.

explanation: Rule: 'A number of' means 'several', so it takes a plural verb. ('The number of' takes a singular verb.)
'volunteers' and 'is volunteering' are singular, so they are out.
The carnival is 'upcoming', so we are talking about something that has happened and still matters now. That is the present perfect: 'have volunteered'.
'had volunteered' (past perfect) is only used for an action that happened before another past action, and there is no other past action here. The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: "Had Sally cut the pineapple earlier, we __________ lost so much time in preparing the dessert," Jenny lamented.

explanation: 'Had Sally cut...' is another way of writing 'If Sally had cut...'. This is the third conditional: it imagines a different past.
Rule: If + had + past participle, ... would (not) have + past participle. It tells us the result that would have happened.
The imagined result is that time was not lost: 'we would not have lost so much time'.
'could not have' would mean it was impossible to lose time, and 'should not have' means it was wrong to. Neither is the plain result of the 'if'. The answer is option (3).

questions.stem: I congratulated Yamal __________ his success winning three gold medals for swimming in the recent National School Games.

explanation: Some verbs always go with a particular preposition. We congratulate someone **on** something.
For example: 'She congratulated me on my results.'
'about' and 'with' are tempting because we say 'happy about' and 'pleased with', but 'congratulate' takes 'on'.
'I congratulated Yamal on his success...' The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: Wenhui saw her classmate __________ into the drain and alerted her teacher immediately.

explanation: Rule: after a verb of the senses (see, hear, watch, feel) + a person or thing, use the base form of the verb (or the -ing form). Example: 'I heard him shout.'
'saw' already shows the past tense, so the second verb is not put into the past again.
'fell' is tempting because the event is in the past, but 'saw her classmate fell' is wrong.
'Wenhui saw her classmate fall into the drain...' The answer is option (1).

questions.stem: Jolin would rather drink green tea __________ jasmine tea.

explanation: Rule: would rather + base verb + **than** ... It shows that one thing is chosen instead of another.
'to' is tempting because we say 'prefer green tea **to** jasmine tea', but 'would rather' pairs with 'than'.
'then' sounds like 'than' but is about time (first this, then that).
'Jolin would rather drink green tea than jasmine tea.' The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: We could smell a strong __________ stench coming from the heap of rubbish as there was a dead rat.

explanation: Clues: a 'stench' is a very bad smell, and it comes from rubbish and a dead rat. We need a word that means disgusting.
'repulsive' means so unpleasant that it makes you want to move away.
'alluring' and 'enticing' both mean attractive and tempting, which is the opposite. 'aggressive' describes behaviour that is ready to attack, not a smell.
The answer is option (3), repulsive.

questions.stem: The students are very fearful of Mrs Lim, the discipline mistress, as they know she is one who should not be __________ with.

explanation: Clue: the students are 'very fearful' of her, so she must be treated seriously.
'to trifle with someone' means to treat them without respect, as if they do not matter. 'Not to be trifled with' is a set phrase for a strict or powerful person.

'meddled with' is tempting, but to meddle means to interfere in something that is not your business. 'dealt with' just means handled, and 'infringe' is used for breaking rules or rights (infringe on).
The answer is option (2), trifled.

questions.stem: My elderly uncle's health has __________ to the point that he is unable to get out of bed by himself.

explanation: Clue: he cannot even get out of bed by himself, so his health has become much worse.
'deteriorated' means became steadily worse in condition. It is the usual word for health getting worse to a serious degree.

'depreciated' is tempting because it also means 'went down', but it is used for the value of money, cars or property. 'declined' is close in meaning, but 'deteriorated' is the more exact word for a condition worsening 'to the point that' something serious happens. 'denominated' is about units of money.
The answer is option (3), deteriorated.

questions.stem: Mr Rogers needed time alone to __________ his decision before making the announcement.

explanation: Clue: he needed 'time alone' before announcing a decision, so he wanted to think about it carefully.
'mull over' means to think about something slowly and carefully.

'weigh down' is tempting because we 'weigh up' choices, but 'weigh down' means to be a heavy burden. 'sink in' means to be slowly understood (the news sank in), and 'revolve around' means to have as the main subject.
The answer is option (2), mull over.

questions.stem: The steep climb to the summit of the mountain was __________ but the boys did not let that affect their spirit.

explanation: Clues: the climb was 'steep', and 'but ... did not let that affect their spirit' tells us it was something hard that could have discouraged them.
'arduous' means very difficult and tiring, needing a lot of effort.

'assiduous' looks similar but describes a person who works very hard and carefully, not a climb. 'ambiguous' means unclear, with more than one meaning. 'adventurous' would not be something that dampens their spirit.
The answer is option (1), arduous.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++finality++.

explanation: To say something 'with finality' is to say it in a way that shows the matter is settled and will not be changed.
Clues in the passage: 'Father had made up his mind' and 'Nothing will change my mind!'
'decisiveness' means the quality of deciding firmly and not wavering, which matches.
'seriousness' is tempting because Father was serious, but a person can be serious and still be undecided. The answer is option (4).

review.note: The key's digit for Q16 is partly under the watermark; the visible strokes are a 4, which matches the solved answer.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++drastically++.

explanation: 'drastically' means in an extreme way that has a very big effect.
The boy sensed his life was about to change in a very big and harsh way, because his beloved Shu Ma was being sent away.
'severely' means very greatly or harshly, so it is the closest. 'subtly' is the opposite (in a small, hardly noticeable way).
'suddenly' is tempting, but it is about how fast a change happens, not how big it is. The answer is option (3).

review.note: The number (17) under 'drastically' is missing in the scan; the word is underlined and sits between (16) and (18), so it is taken as item 17.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++confirmed++.

explanation: To 'confirm' something is to show that it is definitely true.
The boy already feared that Shu Ma would be sent away. When Father said 'Shu Ma will leave tonight', it showed that his fear was true.
'proved' means showed to be true, so it fits: Father proved my worst fears.
'accepted' is tempting, but Father did not agree to the boy's fears; his words showed they were real. The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++outlived++.

explanation: To 'outlive your usefulness' is to go on existing after you have stopped being useful.
'outlive' means to live or last longer than something. 'outlasted' means lasted longer than, so it is the closest.
'outstayed' is tempting because of the phrase 'outstay your welcome', but that means staying in a place longer than you are wanted, which is a different idea.
'outlaid' is about spending money and 'outreached' about reaching further. The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ++sullenly++.

explanation: 'sullenly' means in a bad-tempered, gloomy and unfriendly way.
Clues: Father 'growled' and was 'less understanding' than Ellen, so he was in a bad mood.
'angrily' is the closest in meaning.
'calmly' is the opposite, and 'lowly' means humble or low in rank, not 'in a low voice'. The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about the launch?
options: Reservations for the shoes can be made online.
Only a limited number of shoes will be available.
Anyone can purchase the shoes on 12 December.
Falcon shoes will be sold at all Sports House outlets.

explanation: Check each statement against the poster (Text 1).
The poster says 'A total of 88 pairs will be released.' A fixed, small number means the supply is limited, so statement (2) is true.
(1) is false: 'Reservations and online purchases are not available.' (3) is false: the launch is 'Exclusively for Sports House members'. (4) is false: it is only 'at the Vista City Outlet'.
The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: Although Linda has pain in her knees, she still enjoys her occasional runs at night. Based on Text 1, which two features would benefit Linda most?

explanation: Pick out Linda's two needs: she has knee pain, and she runs at night.
Running at night means low light. Feature D, Visibility: 'Reflective materials keep you visible in low light.'
Knee pain means she must avoid hurting her joints. Feature F, Support: 'Provides stability for injury-free running.'

B (Cushioned Comfort) is tempting, but the poster says it protects the **feet** from blisters, not the knees. She runs only occasionally, so E (Durability) matters less. The answer is option (4), D and F.

questions.stem: What kind of poster is shown in Text 1?

explanation: Ask: what does the poster want the reader to do?
It announces a 'sales launch', gives a price ($129.90), has a catchy slogan ('DON'T RUN, FLY!') and lists the shoe's selling points. It wants people to come and buy the Falcon.
A poster that advertises a product to get people to buy it is promotional.
'informational' is tempting because the poster gives a date and place, but those details serve the main aim, which is to sell. The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is supported by Text 2?
options: All good running shoes prevent runners from getting injured.
The only thing running shoes do is provide runners with comfort.
Choosing a pair of good running shoes is a decision that comes easily to all.
The benefits of proper running shoes are not limited to experienced runners.

explanation: The first sentence of Text 2 says the right shoes are 'important for every runner whether they are experienced athletes or beginners'. So beginners benefit too, which supports (4).
(1) is too strong: the article says shoes help in 'preventing injuries' and lower the 'risk', not that all good shoes stop every injury.
(2) is contradicted: 'Good running shoes do more than keep the feet comfortable.' (3) is contradicted: choosing 'may seem like a simple decision but that is far from the truth'.
Watch out for words like 'all' and 'only'. The answer is option (4).

questions.stem: What message do both Text 1 and Text 2 convey about running shoes?
options: Lightweight shoes are now the best choice for every runner.
Choosing the right running shoes depends on a runner's needs.
The more features a pair of shoes has, the better the shoes are for you.
Shoes with reflective materials are safer than shoes with better cushioning.

explanation: The message must be found in both texts.
Text 1: 'Not every pair is made for the same purpose. Which features would work best for you?'
Text 2: 'Think about the features that will suit you best. Not every runner needs shoes with all sorts of fancy features.'
Both say the right shoe depends on the runner. (3) says the opposite of Text 2, and neither text says lightweight or reflective shoes are best. The answer is option (2).

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (26). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The subject is 'ivory from the mammoth'. The words between the commas ('an extinct ancestor of the elephant') only add information.
After the blank is 'used to make household items'. Ivory does not use anything; it is used by people. That is the passive voice: be + past participle.
'Ivory' is singular and the Stone Age is in the past, so the verb is 'was'.
The answer is (N) was: 'ivory ... was used to make household items'.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (27). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'cool ___ the touch' is a fixed phrase.
We say something is cool, soft or smooth **to the touch**, meaning that is how it feels when you touch it.
The answer is (L) to.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (28). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: Look further along the sentence for a partner word: '___ precious **that** many people referred to it as "white gold"'.
The pattern so + adjective + that shows a result: it was so precious that people called it white gold.
'such' is tempting, but 'such' needs a noun after it (such a precious material that...).
The answer is (H) so.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (29). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: After the blank comes 'as' and then a list of examples: chopsticks, musical instruments and furniture.
'such as' introduces examples of the thing just mentioned ('useful and decorative objects').
The answer is (J) such.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (30). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The second half of the sentence gives the reason for the first half.
Why did wealthy people continue to use ivory as ornaments? They 'regarded it as a symbol of wealth and prestige'.
A connector that introduces a reason is 'because'.
The answer is (D) because.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (31). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: 'sought after' is a fixed phrase meaning wanted by many people. ('sought' is the past participle of 'seek'.)
As demand increased, ivory became 'highly sought after'.
The answer is (A) after.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (32). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The blank comes before a noun phrase ('Asian counterparts'), so we need a word that shows belonging.
The counterparts belong to 'African elephants', which is plural, so the word is 'their'.
'their Asian counterparts' means the Asian elephants, which are the matching animals in Asia.
The answer is (K) their.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (33). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The noun 'ban' takes the preposition 'on': a ban **on** something.
For example: a ban on smoking, a ban on plastic bags.
'an international ban on the ivory trade'. The answer is (G) on.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (34). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The sentence gives a condition and a feared result: stronger efforts to protect elephants / elephants could disappear.
The elephants will disappear only if stronger efforts are **not** made. 'Unless' means 'if ... not'.
'when' and 'after' do not work, because then making stronger efforts would lead to the elephants disappearing.
The answer is (M) unless.

questions.stem: Choose the most suitable word for blank (35). (Type its letter, A to Q.)

explanation: The blank comes before a period of time: 'the next twenty years'.
'within' means before that period of time is over.
'after' has already been used for blank (31), each word can be used only once, and 'within' fits the worry that it could happen soon.
The answer is (Q) within.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (36) ++begin++.

explanation: This is a grammar error. Look at the helping verb in front: 'She **was** ___ to understand'.
Rule: was/were + verb-ing makes the past continuous tense, for something that was happening at that time.
begin + ing: double the 'n' because the stress is on the last syllable: beginning.
The correct word is 'beginning'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (37) ++cabtivatted++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word means held the full attention of someone because it is so interesting.
Say it in syllables: cap-ti-vat-ed. It comes from 'captive' (a prisoner), so it has a 'p', not a 'b'.
There is only one 't' before '-ed': captivate + d.
The correct word is 'captivated'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (38) ++nervous++.

explanation: This is a grammar error (wrong word form). 'nervous' is an adjective.
After a possessive word like 'her', and after 'give in to', we need a noun: give in to her ___.
Add the suffix -ness to turn the adjective into a noun: nervous + ness.
The correct word is 'nervousness'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (39) ++jescher++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The clue is 'a little with her hands': the word means to move your hands to help express what you are saying.
The 'j' sound at the start is spelt with a 'g' (like gentle), and the ending that sounds like 'cher' is spelt '-ture' (like picture, nature).
The correct word is 'gesture'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (40) ++Eloquent++.

explanation: This is a grammar error (wrong word form). 'Eloquent' is an adjective.
The word describes **how** she talked, and a word that describes a verb must be an adverb.
Add -ly to make the adverb. It starts the sentence, so keep the capital letter.
The correct word is 'Eloquently'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (41) ++daspparate++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word means needing something very badly: her father badly needed to make ends meet.
Say it in syllables: des-per-ate. It has one 'p', and the middle is 'per' even though it sounds like 'pruht'.
Do not confuse it with 'separate', which does have '-par-' in the middle.
The correct word is 'desperate'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (42) ++foltor++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The clue is the next sentence: she stammered and could not continue. The word means to lose confidence and hesitate or stop.
The 'ol' sound is spelt 'al' (like alter, salt, halt) and the ending is '-er'.
The correct word is 'falter'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (43) ++stammer++.

explanation: This is a grammar error (tense). The whole passage is told in the past tense: 'When she **started**...', '...and **could** not continue'.
The verb must be in the simple past tense too.
stammer + ed. Do not double the 'r', because the stress is on the first syllable (STAM-mer).
The correct word is 'stammered'.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (44) ++fimilair++.

explanation: This is a spelling error. The word means known to you, seen before.
It comes from the word 'family': fam-il-i-ar. The first vowel is 'a', and the ending is '-iar', not '-air'.
The correct word is 'familiar'.

review.note: In the next sentence of the passage the scan shows a name ('Jamie') struck through by hand; it is transcribed as 'Janet', the only girl in the passage. This does not affect any answer.

questions.stem: Write the correct word for (45) ++to++.

explanation: This is a grammar error (wrong preposition).
The verb 'erupt' takes 'into' when a crowd suddenly starts making a loud noise: erupt into laughter, erupt into cheers, erupt into a roar.
'into' shows a change from one state (quiet) to another (roaring).
The correct word is 'into'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (46) with a suitable word.

explanation: Look back at the first sentence: Singapore imports food 'because of its small land size'.
This sentence repeats that idea: the country's ___ land means farms cannot produce enough food. We need an adjective meaning 'not much'.
'limited' fits best. 'scarce' also carries the same meaning.
The answer is 'limited'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (47) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'As a result' tells us this sentence is the result of local farms not producing enough food.
The first sentence says 'Singapore imports much of its food', and the blank is followed by 'food from many different countries'.
Before the noun 'food' we can use the past participle as an adjective: 'imported food' (food that has been brought in from other countries). 'depends on importing food' is also correct.
The answer is 'imported'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (48) with a suitable word.

explanation: The blank starts a sentence and is followed by a comma, so it is a connector linking this sentence to the one before.
Before: Singapore depends on food from many countries. After: unexpected events may interrupt food supplies. The second sentence brings in a problem, which is a contrast.
The connector for a contrast is 'However'. Remember the capital letter.
The answer is 'However'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (49) with a suitable word.

explanation: Extreme weather, conflicts and disrupted transport routes can cut off food supplies.
The word must go with 'to': 'more ___ to interruptions'. It should mean easily harmed or affected.
'vulnerable to' means exposed to the danger of something. 'susceptible to' and 'prone to' mean the same.
The answer is 'vulnerable'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (50) with a suitable word.

explanation: If food supplies are interrupted, there will not be enough food.
A situation where there is not enough of something is a 'shortage'. 'food shortages' is a common pairing.
There is no 'a' before 'temporary', and it happens in 'some parts of the world', so the plural 'shortages' fits best.
The answer is 'shortages'.

review.keyAnswer: shortage(s) (end of the word is under the watermark)
review.note: The end of the key's word is hidden by the watermark, so both 'shortages' and 'shortage' are accepted.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (51) with a suitable word.

explanation: The blank describes the 'farming methods' Singapore has invested in.
The clue is what these methods do: they 'make better use of every available space', like vertical farming with sensors. They are clever, new ways of farming.
The key's word is 'smarter' (cleverer than the old methods). Words such as 'innovative', 'modern' and 'advanced' give the same meaning and fit the grammar.
The answer is 'smarter'.

review.note: Open cloze: solved as 'innovative'; the key gives 'smarter'. Both fit, so the key's word is the value and close synonyms are accepted.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (52) with a suitable word.

explanation: The sentence contrasts two ways of growing vegetables: 'on stacked shelves' and 'across wide fields'.
The blank is followed by 'of'. The phrase 'instead of' means 'in place of'.
Vegetables are grown on stacked shelves instead of across wide fields.
The answer is 'instead'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (53) with a suitable word.

explanation: The pattern is 'a larger ___ of crops'. We need a noun for how much is produced.
Stacking the shelves lets farmers grow more while 'using much less land', so the contrast is between more crops and less land.
'amount' fits. 'quantity' and 'yield' (how much a farm produces) are also correct.
The answer is 'amount'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (54) with a suitable word.

explanation: Sensors measure light, temperature and humidity. Why? So that the crops get just what they need.
The blank describes the 'amount of water and nutrients': not too little and not too much. The same sentence later mentions 'avoiding unnecessary waste'.
The key's word is 'sufficient' (enough). 'right' or 'correct' is the most natural choice after 'the' and is also accepted.
The answer is 'sufficient'.

review.note: Open cloze: solved as 'right' ('the right amount' is the natural phrase); the key gives 'sufficient'. Both mean the crops get what they need, so the key's word is the value and 'right' and similar words are accepted.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (55) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'As a result' tells us this is the benefit of crops getting enough water and nutrients.
After 'can' we need a base-form verb, and its object is 'the growth of their crops'. With the right water and nutrients, crops grow more.
'increase' fits. 'maximise', 'improve' and 'boost' also work.
The answer is 'increase'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (56) with a suitable word.

explanation: The clue is 'recycle water and use it more efficiently'. Doing this means less water is used up.
After 'helping to' we need a base-form verb whose object is 'valuable natural resources'.
'conserve' means to use carefully so that it is not wasted. 'save' has the same meaning.
The answer is 'conserve'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (57) with a suitable word.

explanation: 'Since the vegetables are grown locally' means they do not travel far, so they get to the supermarkets in a short time.
The blank comes after 'more' and describes the verb 'reach', so it must be an adverb (ending in -ly). 'more fast' and 'more faster' are wrong.
'more quickly' fits, and it explains the 'greater freshness' in the rest of the sentence.
The answer is 'quickly'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (58) with a suitable word.

explanation: The sentence compares local vegetables with vegetables brought from far away.
We need a preposition between 'transported' and 'long distances'. Things travel or are transported **over** long distances.
'across' is also acceptable.
The answer is 'over'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (59) with a suitable word.

explanation: Look at the words around the blank: 'meet the entire ___ for food'.
'meet the demand for' is a common pairing. 'demand' means how much of something people want or need.
The passage earlier said local farms 'cannot produce enough food to feed the entire population', which is the same idea.
The answer is 'demand'.

questions.stem: Fill in blank (60) with a suitable word.

explanation: This sentence sums up the passage: local farms cannot grow everything, but they still play an important role.
How do they help? The passage is about 'food security' and coping with interruptions to supply. So local farms make Singapore's food supply one that can keep going in the future.
'sustainable' means able to continue for a long time. 'secure', 'stable' and 'reliable' also fit.
The answer is 'sustainable'.

questions.stem:
Dave does not turn up for morning exercise. His brothers do not turn up either.
Neither ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: Neither Dave nor his brothers turn up for morning exercise.

explanation: 'Neither ... nor ...' joins two negative statements. It already means 'not', so drop 'does not', 'do not' and 'either'.
Put the two subjects into the pattern: Neither Dave nor his brothers ...
Agreement rule: with neither ... nor, the verb agrees with the subject nearest to it. The nearest subject is 'his brothers' (plural), so the verb is 'turn', not 'turns'.
Keep the present tense. Answer: Neither Dave nor his brothers turn up for morning exercise.

review.keyAnswer: Neither Dave nor his brothers turn up for morning exercise.
review.solvedAnswer: Neither Dave nor his brothers turn up for morning exercise.

questions.stem:
Min wants to perfect his pasta recipe. He also hopes to learn how to make bread.
Other than ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: Other than wanting to perfect his pasta recipe, Min also hopes to learn how to make bread.
accept: Other than wanting to perfect his pasta recipe, Min hopes to learn how to make bread.
Other than wanting to perfect his pasta recipe, Min also hopes to learn how to make bread

explanation: 'Other than' means 'besides' or 'in addition to'. It is a preposition, so the verb after it takes the -ing form (or is replaced by a noun).
Change 'wants' to 'wanting': Other than wanting to perfect his pasta recipe, ...
Put a comma after the opening phrase. Then name the person in the main clause ('Min', not 'He'), because the opening phrase has no subject of its own.
Keep both wishes exactly: 'wants to perfect' and 'hopes to learn'. Answer: Other than wanting to perfect his pasta recipe, Min also hopes to learn how to make bread.

review.keyAnswer: Other than wanting to perfect his paste recipe, Min also hopes to learn how to make bread.
review.solvedAnswer: Other than wanting to perfect his pasta recipe, Min also hopes to learn how to make bread.
review.note: The key writes 'paste recipe', a typing slip for 'pasta recipe' as printed in the question.

questions.stem:
"Where did you hide my toy last week?" Lee asked his sister.
Lee asked ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: Lee asked his sister where she had hidden his toy the previous week.
accept: Lee asked his sister where she had hidden his toy the week before.
Lee asked his sister where she had hidden his toy the previous week

explanation: This is direct speech changed to reported speech. A reported question uses statement word order (subject before verb), has no 'did', and ends with a full stop, not a question mark.
Tense moves one step back: simple past 'did you hide' becomes past perfect 'had hidden'.
Pronouns change to fit the speaker: 'you' is his sister, so 'she'; 'my' is Lee's, so 'his'.
Time words change: 'last week' becomes 'the previous week' or 'the week before'.
Answer: Lee asked his sister where she had hidden his toy the previous week.

review.keyAnswer: Lee asked his sister where she had hidden his toy the previous week.
review.solvedAnswer: Lee asked his sister where she had hidden his toy the previous week.

questions.stem:
Tabitha called the police when she witnessed a robbery.
____________________ upon ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: Tabitha called the police upon witnessing a robbery.
accept: Tabitha called the police upon witnessing a robbery

explanation: 'upon' means 'immediately after' or 'at the moment of'. It replaces 'when'.
'upon' is a preposition, so it is followed by the -ing form of the verb (or a noun), and the subject 'she' is dropped: 'when she witnessed' becomes 'upon witnessing'.
'upon' is in the middle of the answer line, so the main clause comes first and stays the same: Tabitha called the police ...
Answer: Tabitha called the police upon witnessing a robbery.

review.keyAnswer: Tabitha called the police upon witnessing a robbery.
review.solvedAnswer: Tabitha called the police upon witnessing a robbery.

questions.stem:
She worked hard to pursue excellence in her studies.
In her ____________________.
(Rewrite as one sentence using the word(s) given. The meaning must stay the same.)

answer.value: In her pursuit of excellence in her studies, she worked hard.
accept: In her pursuit of excellence in her studies, she worked hard

explanation: After a possessive word like 'her' we need a noun, so the verb 'pursue' must change to its noun form: 'pursuit'.
The noun 'pursuit' takes the preposition 'of': 'to pursue excellence' becomes 'her pursuit of excellence'.
Keep the rest of the phrase ('in her studies'), put a comma, then write the main clause: she worked hard.
Answer: In her pursuit of excellence in her studies, she worked hard.

review.keyAnswer: In her pursuit of excellence in her studies, she worked hard.
review.solvedAnswer: In her pursuit of excellence in her studies, she worked hard.

questions.stem: Based on lines 1 to 8 (paragraph 1), why were visitors impressed by Trev?

answer.value: Visitors were impressed by Trev because he had an extraordinary natural talent for sculpting.

explanation: Find the sentence about visitors in paragraph 1: 'Trev's extraordinary natural talent quickly earned him the admiration of visitors'.
'earned him the admiration of visitors' means the same as 'visitors were impressed by him', so the cause is his extraordinary natural talent.
The marker looks for: extraordinary natural talent (for sculpting). Do not write that he was proud; that was the result of the praise, not the reason for it.

review.keyAnswer: Trev had an extraordinary natural talent for sculpting.
review.solvedAnswer: He had extraordinary natural talent (for sculpting).

questions.stem: Which six-word phrase in Paragraph 3 shows that Dev used his observations to guide his choice of sculpture?

answer.value: Inspired by what he had seen
accept: inspired by what he had seen
Inspired by what he had seen,
inspired by what he had seen,

explanation: In paragraph 3, Dev spends days 'observing ordinary people': labourers and parents caring for their children.
The next sentence links what he saw to what he chose to sculpt: 'Inspired by what he had seen, he decided to sculpt an elderly farmer carrying a tired child'.
Count exactly six words and copy them without changing anything: Inspired (1) by (2) what (3) he (4) had (5) seen (6). Writing more or fewer words loses the mark.
The answer is 'Inspired by what he had seen'.

review.keyAnswer: Inspired by what he had seen
review.solvedAnswer: Inspired by what he had seen

questions.stem: Based on lines 18 to 21 (paragraph 4, from "As the weeks passed" to "smirking with pride"), explain Trev's attitude towards his craft.

answer.value: Trev was only concerned with how his sculpture looked and paid little attention to how well it was made or how long it would last. Whenever cracks or uneven surfaces appeared, he concealed them under carvings instead of repairing them properly.

explanation: An 'explain' question for 2 marks needs two things: what his attitude was, and the evidence from the lines given.

Attitude (1 mark): he cared only about the sculpture's appearance and about impressing people, not about its durability or doing the work properly. Evidence: 'Trev was only concerned with the sculpture's appearance. He paid little attention to its durability.'
Action that shows it (1 mark): he 'worked hastily', and when cracks or uneven surfaces appeared 'he concealed them under carvings instead of repairing them properly'.
Use the name 'Trev' and describe the attitude in your own words (careless about quality, took shortcuts) before giving the evidence.

review.keyAnswer: When crack or uneven surfaces appeared on Trev's craft, Trev would conceal them under carrying [carvings] instead of repairing them properly. This shows that Trev was only concerned with the sculptures appearance and paid lite [little] attention to its durability.
review.solvedAnswer: He cared only about appearance, not durability or proper workmanship: he hid cracks under carvings instead of repairing them. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Look at the table below. What do the words in the left column refer to in the passage? Write your answers in the column on the right.

parts.label: a

answer.value: The competition that the King of Tiwana announced (to select a sculpture for the new Hall of Wisdom).
accept: the competition that the King of Tiwana announced
The competition that the King of Tiwana announced

explanation: A word like 'this' points back to something already mentioned. Read the sentences just before it.

'While many sculptors saw it as a chance to showcase their skills, Trev saw **this** as an opportunity to earn fame.' Both 'it' and 'this' point back to what the King announced in the first sentence of the paragraph.
Test by replacing the word: 'Trev saw the competition as an opportunity to earn fame.' It makes sense.
The answer is the competition announced by the King of Tiwana.

parts.label: b

answer.value: Visitors gravitating towards Trev's (spectacular warrior) sculpture.

explanation: Read the sentence just before 'Seeing **this**': 'When visitors entered the workshop to watch them work, they gravitated towards Trev's spectacular warrior.'
What Trev saw was the visitors being drawn to his sculpture rather than Dev's. That is why he mocked Dev straight after.
'this' here refers to a whole event, not one noun, so the answer must include who (the visitors) and what they did (gravitated or were drawn towards Trev's sculpture).
The answer is the visitors gravitating towards Trev's sculpture.

parts.label: c
explanation: 'he noticed the warmth in the farmer's eyes, the careful shaping of **his** worn hands'.
'his' is tricky because Trev and Dev are also male. Ask: whose worn hands were carefully shaped? The hands are part of the sculpture, like the eyes mentioned just before.
The nearest matching noun before 'his' is 'the farmer'. Earlier, Dev 'carefully carved the farmer's weathered hands'.
The answer is the farmer that Dev sculpted (not Dev and not Trev).

review.keyAnswer: a) The competition that the king of Tiwana announced. b) Visitors gravitating towards Terv's [Trev's] sculpture. c) The farmer that Dev sculpted.
review.solvedAnswer: a) the competition; b) visitors gravitating towards Trev's warrior; c) the farmer. Agrees with key.
review.note: Several phrases of the passage look bold in the scan because a previous owner highlighted them. Only the three referencing words asked about in Q69 (this, this, his) are transcribed as bold.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: What did Trev mean by, "Your sculpture is not getting you anything" (line 25, paragraph 4)?

answer.value: Trev meant that Dev's sculpture would not win the competition (or earn him any fame or reward).

explanation: Think about what there was to 'get': the competition winner would receive 'a royal title and a chest of gold', and Trev saw it as 'an opportunity to earn fame'.
Trev said this right after visitors gravitated towards his warrior, and he added that Dev's 'common man pales in comparison'.
So 'not getting you anything' means Dev's sculpture would not win him the competition, the prize or any recognition.
The marker looks for: Dev's sculpture would not win (the competition / the prize / attention).

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: How can you tell Dev was unaffected by what Trev said in (a)?

answer.value: Dev replied calmly that sometimes ordinary things are what matter most.

explanation: Look at how Dev reacted straight after Trev scoffed: '"Sometimes," Dev replied calmly, "ordinary things are what matter most."'
The key word is 'calmly'. A person who was hurt or angry would not answer calmly, and he also stood by his choice of an ordinary subject.
The marker looks for: Dev replied calmly (and what he said). Quote or retell the line accurately.

review.keyAnswer: a) Trev meant that Dev's sculpture would not win. b) Dev calmly replied that sometimes ordinary [things are what matter most; the key's line is cut short].
review.solvedAnswer: a) Dev's sculpture would not win or earn him anything; b) he replied calmly. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Choose two words from paragraphs 4 and 5 which have similar meanings to the words below.

parts.label: a
explanation: 'magnificence' is a noun meaning the quality of being very grand and impressive. Look for a noun with that meaning.
Paragraph 5: 'Although his sculpture lacked **grandeur**, it moved everyone.' Dev's simple farmer was not grand like Trev's towering warrior.
Test by swapping: 'Although his sculpture lacked magnificence' makes sense. 'spectacular' in paragraph 4 is tempting, but it is an adjective, and the answer must be the same kind of word.
The answer is 'grandeur'. Copy the spelling exactly.

parts.label: b
explanation: 'battered' is an adjective meaning worn and damaged from long, hard use.
Paragraph 4: Dev 'carefully carved the farmer's **weathered** hands'. Weathered hands are rough and worn from years of work in the sun and rain.
'worn' means the same, but it is in paragraph 6, and the question limits you to paragraphs 4 and 5.
The answer is 'weathered'.

questions.stem: Explain fully what Dev meant by "ordinary things are what matter most" in line 27 (paragraph 4).

answer.value: Dev meant that ordinary people and everyday things, like the elderly farmer carrying a tired child, may not look impressive, but they are more meaningful and important than grand, impressive things like Trev's towering warrior.

explanation: 'Explain fully' for 2 marks means two ideas are needed, and you must say what 'ordinary things' are in this story.
Idea 1: 'ordinary things' are everyday people and scenes, like his elderly farmer carrying a tired child. They are simple and not impressive to look at. (Trev had just called it a 'common man'.)
Idea 2: 'matter most' means they are the most meaningful or valuable, more than grand and showy things such as Trev's towering warrior.
The ending proves him right: the sculpture 'lacked grandeur' but 'it moved everyone'.

review.keyAnswer: Ordinary people like farmer or everyday things are not impressive but they are more meaningful than towering warriors.
review.solvedAnswer: Simple, everyday people and things (like the farmer) are more meaningful than grand, impressive ones (like the warrior). Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Based on evidence from the text, explain how Trev felt when his sculpture shattered. (lines 31 to 33, paragraph 5, from "Moments later" to "across the ground")

answer.value: Trev felt embarrassed (ashamed). His face turned beetroot red and he lowered his head as the broken pieces lay scattered across the ground.

explanation: This needs a feeling (1 mark) and the evidence for it (1 mark).
Evidence: 'Trev's face turned beetroot red and he lowered his head as the broken pieces lay scattered across the ground.'
A face turning red and a lowered head are signs of embarrassment or shame. It happened in front of the judges and a courtyard full of spectators, and his 'hidden flaws ... had finally been exposed'.
Name the feeling with a precise word (embarrassed, ashamed, humiliated), not just 'sad' or 'bad', then quote the evidence.

review.keyAnswer: Trev felt embarrassed. Trev's face turned beetroot red and he lowered his head as the broken pieces lay scattered across the ground.
review.solvedAnswer: Embarrassed or ashamed; his face turned beetroot red and he lowered his head. Agrees with key.

questions.stem: Based on lines 28 to 46 (paragraphs 5 to 7), state whether each statement in the table below is true or false, then give one reason why you think so.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Part of Trev's sculpture crumbled to the ground during the inspection.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: True. A large fracture spread across the statue's chest before both of its arms broke away (and the broken pieces lay scattered across the ground).

explanation: Find the inspection in paragraph 5: 'just as they were inspecting it, a faint crack echoed through the courtyard. Moments later, a large fracture spread across the statue's chest before both of its arms broke away.'
'Part of' matches 'both of its arms', 'crumbled to the ground' matches 'the broken pieces lay scattered across the ground', and 'during the inspection' matches 'just as they were inspecting it'.
So the statement is True. The reason must be evidence from the passage, not the statement repeated.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
Trev's sculpture attracted more spectators than Dev's on the day of judgement.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: False. Both sculptures had their own set of admirers.

explanation: Paragraph 5 describes the spectators on the day of judgement: 'Both sculptures had their own set of admirers.'
Nothing says Trev's had more on that day. The trap is paragraph 4, where visitors 'gravitated towards Trev's spectacular warrior', but that was earlier, in the workshop.
So the statement is False, and the reason is that both sculptures had their own set of admirers.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt:
Trev finally understood the true meaning of the competition after Master Govin's reminder.
(Type True or False, then give one reason from the passage.)

answer.value: False. Trev had already realised it when he studied Dev's sculpture, before Master Govin came into the workshop. Master Govin's words only reinforced that realisation; they did not cause it.

explanation: Look at the order of events in paragraph 6. First Trev studied Dev's sculpture: 'Seeing that, realisation finally dawned on him; it was never just about the end result.'
Only after that: 'Master Govin **then** came into the workshop and reminded him...'. The word 'then' shows the reminder came after the realisation.
So Trev understood before the reminder, not after it. The statement is False.
Reason: the realisation dawned on Trev when he studied Dev's sculpture; Master Govin's words came afterwards and only reinforced it.

review.keyAnswer: a) True --- A large fracture spread across the statue's chest before both of its arms broke away. b) False --- Both sculptures had their own set of admirers. c) False --- Master Govin words reinforced that realisation, they did not cake [cause] it.
review.solvedAnswer: a) True; b) False; c) False (realisation dawned on him before Master Govin came in). Agrees with key.
review.note: The words True/False in the key are partly under the watermark but readable. The key's 'did not cake it' is read as 'did not cause it'.

questions.stem:
"It was never just about the end result." (lines 39 to 40, paragraph 6)
How did Trev's view of Dev's sculpture change after the competition?

answer.value: Initially, Trev believed that only appearance mattered, so he looked down on Dev's sculpture as ordinary and unimpressive. After the competition, he saw the warmth, careful work and quiet beauty in it, and realised that the patience and process (the journey) that went into a sculpture were important too.

explanation: A 'how did it change' question needs both sides: the view before (1 mark) and the view after (1 mark).
Before: Trev mocked Dev's 'ordinary subject' and said the 'common man pales in comparison to my towering warrior'. He believed only an impressive appearance and the end result mattered.

After: 'For the first time, he noticed the warmth in the farmer's eyes, the careful shaping of his worn hands and the quiet beauty that could only come from patience.' He realised 'it was never just about the end result': the process, patience and care mattered too.
Use signal words such as 'Initially ... After the competition ...' so the marker can see the change.

review.keyAnswer: Initially, he believed that it is only appearances matter. After the competition, he realised that the journey/ process of the competition was of equal/ the importance too.
review.solvedAnswer: Before: he scorned it as ordinary because only looks and the end result mattered to him. After: he appreciated its warmth and quiet beauty and saw that patience and the process mattered. Agrees with key.
review.note: The key's sentence is loosely worded ('was of equal/ the importance too') and its first words are under the watermark. The model answer keeps the key's two points (only appearance mattered; then the journey or process mattered too) and ties them to Dev's sculpture, as the question asks.
